name: Closest Without Going Over
why_it_works: A price is a number everyone has an opinion on, so guessing costs nothing and feels like winning. The 'without going over' rule makes people think about value instead of throwing out a random number, and holding the answer back gives them a reason to come back for the reveal post.

hook.pattern: Show the item with the price tag face-down and dare the viewer to guess it.
examples: Guess the price. Closest without going over wins it.
This {{product}} has a price. You have one guess.
Nobody has guessed this price right yet. Your turn.

variables.name: product
variables.description: The single item people will price

variables.name: clue
variables.description: One honest clue that hints at the value
variables.example: it took 11 hours at the bench

variables.name: decoy_price
variables.description: An anchor price to guess higher or lower against

variables.name: real_price
variables.description: The actual price, revealed only in the carousel or follow-up post

variables.name: prize
variables.example: the ring itself, sized to fit

variables.name: deadline
variables.description: When guesses close and the answer drops

craft.notes: The decoy price gives people a reference point so guesses cluster and arguments start in the comments. The reel never shows the real price; the carousel or a follow-up post does, which turns one ad into a two-post series.

do_not: Reveal the price in the reel itself; it kills the reason to comment
Use a fake or inflated 'real price' to make the item look like a steal
Run the prize without stating the end date and how the winner is chosen
compliance: Giveaways: state 'no purchase necessary', eligibility (age and location), the end date and how the winner is picked
Say the promotion is not sponsored or run by the platform
